question: Should the new public `agents set-default` command be accepted as the supported replacement for manual default-agent config edits once its source/runtime config boundary is repaired?
rationale: The mechanical lookup repair is clear, but the PR also introduces a public CLI contract and changes the documented default-marker policy; the `maintainer` label calls for an explicit decision on that operator-facing direction.

options.title: Sponsor the command with the compatibility repair
options.body: Keep the command, validate against the normalized roster, preserve serialized config on write, and document the existing fallback behavior unless a separate migration is approved.

options.title: Require an invariant migration first
options.body: Adopt the exactly-one-default policy only with explicit validation, upgrade migration, and compatibility proof for existing configs.

options.title: Retain the manual configuration workflow
options.body: Decline the new CLI surface and restore documentation describing the supported existing configuration behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the command with the compatibility repair
recommendation.body: Keep the command, validate against the normalized roster, preserve serialized config on write, and document the existing fallback behavior unless a separate migration is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The available change history ties this contributor directly to the proposed agent CLI surface and its intended operator contract.
